scenes.line1: How do you stop API abuse?
scenes.say: How do you stop API abuse and keep your services reliable? Let’s break down rate limiting and API gateways.

scenes.label: Limiter
scenes.sub: Restricts how often clients call your API.
scenes.say: Rate limiting simply means restricting how often clients can call your API.
An API gateway centralizes key tasks: authentication, routing, and rate limiting. It’s your control point for protecting services.

scenes.title: Nginx Rate Limit
scenes.say: Here’s how Nginx can enforce limits, or you can set a gateway to allow one thousand requests per minute per user.

scenes.label: Back-pressure
scenes.sub: Signals clients to slow down if overloaded.
scenes.say: Back-pressure is key. When overloaded, your system tells clients to slow down, preventing crashes.

scenes.question: Where should you enforce rate limits?
scenes.right: At the API gateway, so all traffic is controlled before hitting services.
scenes.say: Don’t just rate limit each backend. Always enforce limits at the API gateway, so all traffic is controlled up front.
